findings.title: External item 0 names the surface with a `<name>` placeholder in a reference that substitutes `<change-name>`
findings.recommendation: Every other placeholder in REVIEW_EXTERNAL_MODE_SECTIONS_REFERENCE (the system read list two lines above, the commit-range command) is `<change-name>`; the new item 0 alone writes `orbit status --change <name> --scenarios --json`. The packaging AI substitutes the change name into the prompt, and a substitution keyed on the reference's placeholder leaves `<name>` literal, so the external reviewer either guesses the name or runs a command that fails and — per the item's own fallback — reports the check as not run, which is exactly the Pass 0 reader exit (2) is meant to make work. Write `<change-name>` in item 0, and move the `orbit-verify-modifications` `Every Pass 0 reader reads the scenario map` external row and its scenario plus the verify-scenario-map.test.ts item-0 assertion to the same spelling (or state in the requirement that the placeholder follows the prompt's own convention).

findings.title: `Emit scope` still calls `orbit-sync-specs` "upstream primitive, unmodified by orbit"
findings.recommendation: Task 4.3's apply note repaired this exact claim in `orbit-conventions`' `Upstream-verbatim — kept unchanged` (sync-specs carries a `# Orbit additions` section with the epitome and the consent note). The same capability this change already modifies keeps the sibling statement in `Emit scope`. Either narrow it to "upstream primitive whose upstream portion orbit does not edit; no emit behavior is added to it" and point at `Generated-file disposition`, or record it as a known residual at archive.

findings.title: The stage's rider says a title containing ` :: ` renders ORPHAN; the shipped pin shows it renders MALFORMED
findings.recommendation: The rc06b rider states both unkeyable shapes render ORPHAN. The change's own rider pin (test/core/scenario-map.test.ts, the separator-title test) asserts the tag is MALFORMED and orphans is empty; only the repeated-title shape pairs. The stage's Shipped-as paragraph at archive should say the rider's premise was half false, so the doc does not keep the stronger claim as living prose.

commentary: Pass 0 ran verify-change's procedure through the shipped step 6: the map reads ON, every delta scenario declared (no uncovered, orphan or malformed entry), counts printed as counts, validate clean, and the full suite green — so this pass is itself the first observation of exit (2) on the internal side. The upstream-portion measurement behind the narrowed `Generated-file disposition` was re-run independently (each of the ten upstream/v1.3.1 bodies diffed against its portion before `# Orbit additions`, rename normalized): only apply-change and archive-change carry edits besides verify's new one, matching the named limit. The reader table is a byte-equal mirror and every JSON field and source variant the surface can return (tag, ledger, ledger-file, spec) has a row. Lenses are absent, so Passes 4 and 5 did not run; Pass 6 was the source lint plus targeted residue greps for the retired phrases (only the baselines carry them, as the at-archive note expects), not a full audit-drift run.

direction.reasoning: The mechanism is small, entirely prose plus tests, and the parts that could silently drift — the reader table, the hash pins, the upstream-edit limit — are each held by a check or a re-measurable fact. The one real gap is a placeholder spelling in the external item 0 that can make the external Pass 0 reader fail to run the command it was given; it is a one-line repair with its spec row and test, and does not need another design round.
